method:
Scorecard: do the research and the trades add value? Usage (from the valuation folder): python3 scoring/scorecard.py D

Writes scoring/scorecard.json for market date D and prints a short summary. Two parts:

forecasts  From scoring/live_scores.json (score_live.py is run first if that file is not for D). 12-month forecasts
           whose research leg was the driver model only (runs/<as_of>/<SYM>/result.json research_leg.source ==
           'standard_model'; Kilian 2026-11-04; the 1-month row was dropped): mean CRPS (log-price units, lower is better) of the options market alone
           (p_market), the agents alone after Platt scaling (p_llm_platt) and the published blend (p_final), and the
           agents-minus-market CRPS difference with a standard error clustered by forecast date (names forecast on the
           same date move together, so forecast dates are the independent units).

live_book  The real book rebuilt day by day from data/trades.json (the owner's fills) and data/book.json, from the
           close before the first fill to D. Stocks are marked at the daily close; cash (in the account and the outside
           cash in book.json external_cash) earns the 3M T-bill (../portfolio/data/tbill_3m_weekly.csv, notional,
           calendar days / 365); dividends (../portfolio/data/dividends.json) are credited on the ex-date. Outside money
           (book.json external_cash and lots bought outside the project, funding "external") enters as a cash flow at
           the start of the day it joined the book, valued at the prior close; returns are time-weighted (each day's
           return = value at close / (prior close value + flow at the open) - 1), so added money is not counted as return.
           Two returns:
             whole_book   time-weighted, the whole account, cash included: r = V_close / (V_prior + outside money at the open) - 1.
           invested_cash  return on invested cash, dollar-weighted (Kilian 2026-11-04): the stock sleeve's dollar gain
                          over the period / its average capital, capital_t = S_prior + purchases (own buys at the fill
                          price, outside lots at the prior close, at the open; sales leave at the close). SPY and equal
                          weight are put on the same capital_t on the same days, so the gaps compare the same dollars.
           Whole book is compared with:
             spy              SPY close-to-close plus distributions reinvested on the ex-date (no adjusted closes in the
                              data; dividends.json supplies SPY distributions). Fully invested, so flows do not matter.
             equal_weight     equal weight in the names the real book holds; rebalanced to equal weight at the close on
                              any day the set of names changes and on the first trading day of each month, drifting
                              otherwise; holds T-bill cash while the book holds no stock. Fully invested otherwise.
           A few weeks of daily returns cannot separate skill from luck: the numbers say what happened, not whether it
           will happen again.

(2026-11-04, Kilian: the Standard model trial row and the 1-month forecast row are no longer shown or written.)

12m.status: First 12-month driver-model forecasts mature 2027-10-19; nothing scored yet.

invested_cash.meaning: dollar gain on stocks (price, dividends, realized and unrealized) / average dollars in stocks; SPY and equal weight = the same dollars on the same days in them instead

live_book.spy_basis: price plus distributions reinvested on the ex-date (dividends.json); no adjusted closes in the data
live_book.dividends_missing_note: names not in dividends.json are treated as paying nothing
live_book.note: 31 trading days of returns cannot show skill: daily stock returns swing by about 1-2%, so a gap of a few percent over a few weeks is well within luck. rough_se treats days as independent; read the gaps as what happened, not as evidence, until there are many months. Whole book: time-weighted, cash at the T-bill, vs fully invested SPY and equal weight. Invested cash: dollar-weighted on the stock sleeve, vs the same dollars in SPY and equal weight.
